experiments/star-field/engine/frame/camera.ts

Camera-side per-frame behavior — world/screen anchor
Source src/experiments/star-field/engine/frame/camera.ts
UX surface Boot surfaces: what the user sees first on each bundle.

Members

anchorScreenPos

Projects an anchor's world position into canvas-space pixels for the hover tooltip + leader line — one getWorldPosition → project(camera) → NDC → px pass, all on the shared scratch vector (zero per-frame allocation). Returns null when the anchor or camera isn't projectable (test mocks, unbooted state) or the point sits behind the camera.

  • @param anchor Any Object3D in the scene graph.
  • @param s Engine state (camera + canvas for the projection + size).

worldScreenPos

Projects a raw world point into canvas-space pixels — the projection backing for the navigator-hover position hint. Unlike anchorScreenPos (which bails when the body leaves the view frustum), this always returns a usable position: behind-camera points are mirrored through the screen centre so the clamp lands on the edge facing the object, and any off-screen result is clamped inside SF_TIP.EDGE_PAD — the hint therefore locates the body at any zoom level. edge reports the clamp and angle the outward direction in degrees (canvas coords, y-down) for the leader-line arrow.

  • @param p World-space point (pinned-frame coords).
  • @param s Engine state (camera + canvas for the projection + size).

anchorWorldPos

World position of an anchor — single getWorldPosition call-site so the armed Vector3 stays private to this module; returns {x,y,z} so callers never handle three types.

  • @param anchor Any Object3D in the scene graph.

rotateStarCamera

Arrow-key orbit — rotates the camera around the controls target in screen-intuitive steps: left/right change azimuth, up/down change polar (clamped off the poles so the view can never flip over the top). Pure spherical math on the offset vector — no three types needed — and any running fly-to is cancelled so manual control always wins. The offset is converted to spherical coordinates (r, θ azimuth in the XZ plane, φ polar from +Y), the deltas are applied, then converted back to Cartesian around the target.

  • @param s Engine state (camera + controls required; no-op before boot).
  • @param dAzimuth Azimuth delta in radians (left = -, right = +).
  • @param dPolar Polar delta in radians (down = -, up = +).

handleStarResize

Resize step: measures the shadow host first, then the canvas parent, then the window. Pixel ratio caps at 2 to prevent 3x-phone fill-rate blowout.

  • @param s Engine state.

followSelected

Orbit-follow — keeps the followed anchor pinned at the world origin by counter-translating s.world (the floating origin). Rider-mounted bodies translate ~16k units/s on the galactic ring; riding them by translating the camera would push every coordinate to ~6.7M where float32 quantization (±0.5 units) makes each mesh visibly jitter. Shifting the world instead of the camera yields identical relative motion — the user's orbit/zoom offset is preserved because neither camera nor target moves — while rendered coordinates stay small. Runs before updateFly each tick so the tween's track() resolves inside the pinned frame (select→glide becomes a local move, not a galactic transit). The controls target snaps to the pin only once no fly tween owns it, so orbiting still circles the body while the tween's own target lerp stays free to pan. Registry ids carry no anchor — they are static shard points — and are skipped. Runs every tick (not just post-fly) so the repin lands the same frame a new follow is armed.

  • @param s Engine state.
